text:
Sam: Heads up — since ~02:15 UTC we're seeing intermittent DNS failures from the apac edge pool. Kubernetes node provisioning stalls because image pulls and model checkout hit NXDOMAIN for registries and internal service names.
Anita: Same for us on staging. Kubelet logs show `lookup gcr.io: no such host` then a few seconds later the same query succeeds.
Jia: I captured a quick dig trace from one edge node:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.14-Ubuntu <<>> +time=2 +tries=1 gcr.io @10.1.2.3
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;gcr.io.                        IN      A
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
io.                    300     IN      SOA     ns1.internal. hostmaster.internal. 2026031801 7200 3600 1209600 300
;; Query time: 1 msec
;; SERVER: 10.1.2.3#53(10.1.2.3)
;; WHEN: Wed Mar 18 02:22:14 UTC 2026
```
Then 4s later the same dig returns an ANSWER with A records.
Matt: Noticed we run systemd-resolved on hosts and forward to an egress pool of dnsmasq/stub-forwarders in apac. Also we have nscd on some images for name service caching. Negative caching (nscd) TTL defaults to 3600s — could be serving stale NXDOMAINs for split-horizon names when forwarder rotatation happens.
Anita: Our /etc/resolv.conf points to 127.0.0.53 (systemd-resolved). nsswitch: "hosts: files dns myhostname". There's also nscd running inside container images for faster lookups. Double caching is a smell.
infra-bot: [alert] egress-resolver-errors: 32 events in 5m for apac-edge-pool
Sam: Hypothesis: forwarder rotation + split-horizon (internal answers on some forwarders, NXDOMAIN on others) + negative caching in nscd leads to transient but long-lived NXDOMAINs on nodes that hit the wrong forwarder first.
Jia: Repro steps I used:
1) force query to forwarder A (returns NXDOMAIN)
2) restart dnsmasq on forwarder A to rotate to B
3) immediately query from node — still NXDOMAIN until nscd negative TTL expires
Workaround: `systemctl restart nscd` clears negative cache.
Matt: For immediate mitigation I can push a daemonset that restarts nscd on affected nodes (or remove nscd). Longer term: reduce negative_cache TTL on nscd config or disable negative caching on image build.
OpsOncall: I'll roll a small daemonset to staging to restart nscd every 30s on join for a few mins, then escalate to prod if it looks good. Also adding retry backoff to node-allocator so transient NXDOMAIN doesn't permanently fail provisioning.
Anita: We should also enable DNS query logging on the apac forwarders and add a metric for NXDOMAIN rate per forwarder IP. If some forwarders are consistently authoritative for internal zones, they need sticky routing (keepalive) or we must sync views.
Sam: Agreed. Action items:
- Matt: deploy daemonset to staging to clear nscd negative cache (now)
- Jia: collect mtr/dig traces + packet capture on 10 nodes and upload to S3 (next 30m)
- OpsOncall: add retry tolerance in node-provisioner (PR in ~2h)
- Infra team: audit forwarder config and split-horizon view consistency; consider lowering nscd negative-cache-ttl or disable it in images
- Product infra: monitor NXDOMAIN rate and correlate with node-provision failures
Jia: One more note — glibc has its own resolver behaviour (single-request vs multi-request). We saw some clients choose UDP/TCP differences. If we flip `options single-request-reopen` in resolv.conf it changes behaviour for legacy clients.
Sam: Good catch. Let's avoid hasty global flips; start with the daemonset and improved telemetry. If anyone sees a node stuck in provisioning, run `systemctl restart nscd` as a manual workaround and add `--image-pull-retries 5` to the provisioner for now.
Anita: pinging @networking-team for forwarder logs and @security to ensure DNS logging is OK for internal zones (:eyes:)
Matt: Rolling to staging now. Will post results in 15m.
OpsOncall: Thx — keeping an eye on alerts. :thumbsup:
